# Who we work with

### **Trusted foam conversion experts for the most demanding sectors**

At Kewell Converters, we work with customers who demand precision, reliability, and performance. As
an independent foam converter with over 50 years of experience, we specialise in delivering bespoke
foam solutions for complex, high-spec applications — particularly in the military, defence,
aerospace, and industrial sectors.

We partner with our clients to solve technical challenges, manage the supply chain, and deliver
custom, [high-quality][58] foam components that perform under pressure.

[Laser engraving on closed cell foam, high density polyethylene uses.]

## **Our clients: from global OEMs to emerging innovators**

We’ve worked with more than 3,000 companies over five decades, ranging from niche product developers
to major international manufacturers. Our clients include:
* OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers in aerospace, defence, and automotive
* Military and defence contractors working on land, air, and naval platforms
* Industrial manufacturers requiring custom foam inserts and seals
* Aviation businesses developing cabin components and protective packaging
* Tech startups and scaleups seeking engineered foam for specialist products
* Medical and hygiene product manufacturers using high-performance foams

Every project is different, and so is every solution we deliver.

## **The industries we serve**

We’re focused on sectors where performance, quality, and durability are non-negotiable. Our foam
products are used in environments where failure isn’t an option. We specialise in:

[Royal Air Force Tornado] [Plane landed on the runway] [tooling insert made out of closed cell foam]
[medical pack with foam insert] [Specialised foam insert for medical industry]

### **Military & defence**

From rugged foam inserts for field equipment to shock-absorbing packaging and EMI shielding, we
manufacture specialised foam parts that meet stringent defence requirements.

[Find out more][59]

### **Aerospace & aviation**

Our lightweight foam materials help reduce weight without compromising strength or performance.
Ideal for cabin components, cargo protection, and custom foam inserts.

[Find out more][60]

### **Industrial manufacturing**

We support engineers and procurement teams with engineered foam solutions that improve durability,
ease of assembly, and operational efficiency.

[Industrial Engineering][61]

### **Electronics & technology**

We produce protective foam enclosures, gaskets, and foam shapes that shield sensitive components
from impact, vibration, or static.

### **Medical & hygiene**

Using high-quality foam materials like branded Zotefoams, we manufacture products suitable for
cleanroom environments, sterilisation, and patient handling.

[Find out more][62]

## **More than a manufacturer – a long-term partner**

At Kewell Converters, we don’t just cut foam. We add value at every stage:
* Full CAD design service included as standard to optimise fit and reduce waste
* Expert guidance on foam materials, tolerances and finishing
* Seamless communication with your engineering and production teams
* Manufacturing capabilities that adapt to project complexity and scale
* Supply chain management – we’ll coordinate sourcing, production and delivery for you

By handling more of the project in-house, we reduce complexity and give your team time back to focus
on the bigger picture.

[ready for lamination, laminating process allows for any thickness to be converted into any product]

## **Why procurement teams trust Kewell Converters**

Our reputation has been built on delivering:
* Consistency – [ISO 9001:2015][63] certified processes ensure repeatable quality
* Responsiveness – we collaborate closely with procurement and technical leads
* Expertise – 50 years working with foam only, not rubber or other materials
* Independence – we’re not tied to specific suppliers and always recommend what’s best for your
project

We’re proud to be the UK’s most experienced independent foam fabricator, trusted to deliver
manufactured foam solutions that meet both performance and commercial targets.

If you’re looking for a **custom foam partner** who understands your industry’s challenges, let’s

add value to your next project.

# Sustainability

[[Various foam materials like eva material, LD45 closed cell polyethylene foam scraps and residue,

## **Benefits of our Environmental Management System (EMS):**

Our ISO 14001 (EMS) has brought tremendous advantages to our foam operations. By adopting this
globally recognised standard, we’ve:
* Significantly reduced our environmental impact, aligning our processes with sustainable practices
that benefit both the planet and our customers
* Generated greater efficiency in resource use and waste management ensuring that we minimise
unnecessary consumption, reflecting our commitment to responsible manufacturing

Implementing an EMS allows us to achieve notable cost savings by streamlining operations and
reducing waste-related expenses. Through these strategies, we strive to create a better, more
sustainable future for everyone, ensuring our foam fabrication processes stand as a benchmark in
responsible production practices.

[View our ISO 14001 Certificate here ][59]

## **Our commitment to sustainable practices**

At Kewell Converters, we’re dedicated to reducing our carbon footprint, working towards net-zero,
and continuously improving our environmental performance. As part of this commitment, we’re
registered with [Zellar][60], an online platform that helps us track, manage, and amplify our
sustainability efforts.

We adhere to a comprehensive [Environmental Policy Statement][61], ensuring responsible waste
disposal, pollution reduction, and compliance with environmental regulations. Recycling wherever
possible and assessing the environmental impact of our products and services are key priorities. We
also consider the effects of our operations on the local community and the industries we serve,
taking a proactive approach to sustainability.

We actively promote environmental awareness among our staff, suppliers, contractors, and partners,
ensuring that sustainability remains a shared responsibility.

#### “**At Kewell Converters Ltd, we believe that tackling climate change is not just a global
#### necessity—it’s a local responsibility. As a company rooted in innovation, we are committed to
#### reducing our environmental impact and contributing positively to the communities around us. By
#### embracing technology in all its forms, and through our partnership with the Zellar platform, we
#### are turning sustainability into measurable action—because a better future is one we must all
#### help to shape**“

Marcos Kewell, Joint Managing Director & Zellar Sustainability Champion

[Check out Zellar][62]

At Kewell Converters, we prioritise resource efficiency by optimising product design to maximise
yields and minimise waste. The majority of our foams are sourced from Zotefoams UK, a manufacturer
based less than 20 miles away in Croydon, South London, reducing transport emissions and supporting
local supply chains.

As part of our Environmental Policy Statement, we’re committed to allocating the necessary resources
to achieve our sustainability goals. By continually refining our processes and making responsible
sourcing decisions, we ensure that environmental impact is considered at every stage of production.

Kewell Converters is committed to reducing waste through dedicated recycling initiatives. We have a
weekly recycling collection and also ensure that large amounts of foam waste are redirected for
repurposing rather than disposal. By operating within a closed-loop system, we maximise material
reuse, minimising environmental impact. These efforts align with our commitment to sustainability
and responsible manufacturing.

We actively reduce energy consumption through smart infrastructure choices. We’ve installed MCBD
lighting across our premises, cutting power usage and lowering CO₂ emissions. Additionally, cavity
wall insulation, enhanced roof lights, and cladding improve insulation, reducing the need for
excessive heating and cooling.

We’re committed to green energy solutions, reducing reliance on non-renewable sources. We’ve
installed a 50kWp PV solar panel system with 200 European-made panels, supplying 20% of our power
needs. This investment cuts our CO₂ emissions by 26 tonnes annually, contributing to a cleaner, more
sustainable future.

# Meet the team

[[Our skilled engineers deep in discussion in the factory]][58]

## Family-run business

Explore the vibrant culture of Kewell Converters, a second-generation, family-run business based in
Kent. At Kewell Converters, we believe our 30+ members of staff are our greatest asset. We’ve
created an environment where they feel appreciated, valued, and empowered to excel. Join us as our
managing directors share insights into the culture that drives innovation and excellence in foam
conversion.

### Nick Kewell
### Managing Director

][59]

### Nick Kewell
### Managing Director

An esteemed graduate in Civil Engineering from the University of Birmingham, Nick became a pivotal
part of Kewell Converters in 1998. Bringing with him a profound depth of industrial knowledge
coupled with dynamic leadership attributes, Nick has since sculpted an Operations and Production
team that stands exemplary in the industry.

Beyond orchestrating the meticulous manufacturing and timely dispatch of top-tier foam products,
Nick has a penchant for endurance sports. Often, he can be spotted navigating the picturesque roads
of Kent, gearing up for marathon and endurance challenges. Off the professional grid, he’s a devoted
family man, blessed with three wonderful children. Nick’s past accolades include leading teams as a
captain at the Warlingham Rugby Club, and he still occasionally graces its fields. Beyond the play,
he’s known for his sage advice and uplifting words, often shared over friendly gatherings at the
bar.

[foam manufacturer uk]

### Marcos Kewell
### Director & Special Projects

][60]

### Marcos Kewell
### Director & Special Projects

[foam manufacturer uk]

Armed with an honours degree in Mechanical Engineering, Marcos embarked on an illustrious journey in
the corporate engineering landscape, collaborating with notable entities such as Astra Zeneca Plc.
In 2004, he integrated his expertise with the Kewell Converters family business. Currently, Marcos
spearheads the Commercial and Business Development divisions, nurturing pivotal relationships with
our esteemed customers and suppliers.

In his leisure, Marcos reminisces about his days as a county rugby and water-polo enthusiast. Today,
he continues to make sporting appearances, joining the Old Wilsonian Football Club’s veterans and
indulging in weekly 5-aside football escapades. As he ventures into mastering the intricate nuances
of golf, Marcos simultaneously cherishes family life with his wife and three children. He plays an
instrumental role in directing Kewell Converters’ growth trajectory, working alongside his brother,
Nick Kewell, in fostering a culture of innovation and excellence.

### Neil Johnston
### General Manager

][61]

### Neil Johnston
### General Manager

Joining Kewell Converters in 2018, Neil boasts an impressive track record of nearly three decades in
engineering sales and manufacturing, with specialization in the non-ferrous metals and
thermoplastics sectors. His multifaceted expertise spans from procurement and sales to adept
production and warehouse management. Neil jestingly attributes his comprehensive
experience—symbolized by the many hats he’s worn—to his thinning hair.

Outside of his professional commitments, Neil cherishes moments with his three adult children and
two grandchildren. Whether it’s enjoying serene moments with his wife in local coffee shops,
observing the ebb and flow of life, or navigating the local countryside with his trusty cocker
spaniel by his side, Neil embraces a balanced blend of work and leisure.

### Quality, Health & Safety Manager (QHS Manager)

[Geoff Daniels, quality manager]

Geoff graced Kewell Converters with his presence in September 2020, enriched with an astounding 45
years in the engineering domain. Notably, 26 of those years were dedicated to pivotal Quality roles.
With a diverse professional background spanning defence, retail, and electronics sectors and having
held various managerial positions, Geoff stands as an invaluable pillar of our organisation.

In his capacity at Kewell Converters, Geoff seamlessly amalgamates Quality Assurance and Quality
Control. He fosters a collaborative environment, working hand in hand with the shop floor teams,
facilitating training, and driving process enhancements with collective team input.

Beyond the confines of work, Geoff’s passions lie in the realm of motorsport and the restoration of
vintage bicycles. He’s also an avid metal detector enthusiast, jestingly on the lookout for his next
big find. A loyal supporter of Charlton Athletics, Geoff’s most cherished moments are spent with his
young granddaughter, creating memories to last a lifetime.

Scot has built an impressive career over 25 years in the foam and rubber industry, evolving into a
respected Technical Sales Manager at Kewell Converters. His professional journey is a testament to
his commitment and passion for engineering and problem-solving, beginning on the factory floor and
advancing through dispatch to excel in sales and business development. Scot’s expertise in foam
fabrication and converting is complemented by his dedication to customer satisfaction and leadership

Outside of work, Scot is a devoted family man, balancing his thriving career with personal interests
such as playing golf, watching football, cooking and baking—where he enjoys the technical precision

solutions drives his ambition to deliver impactful, technically engineered foam solutions that set
industry standards.

# Quality at Kewell Converters

Kewell Converters is committed to delivering high-quality foam solutions to a vast variety of
sectors. Central to our success is our focus on quality, which we believe is crucial not just in
producing outstanding foam products but in fostering long-term relationships with our clients.

By prioritising excellence in every aspect of production, we ensure that our customers receive
unparalleled service and products that set the standard in the field.

> "Quality is one of the cornerstones of the Kewell ideology. It’s why many of our customers come
> back time and time again. We use various measures to ensure that parts we make are of the highest
> quality. Whether it’s taking and documenting part dimensions at every step of the manufacturing
> process or ensuring that all our machinery is in the very best condition. Quality is our compass,
> guiding us in every decision and action we take."

Neil Johnson General Manager

## Backed by ISO accreditations

Furthering customers’ peace of mind are certifications from [ISO 9001: 2015][58] Quality Management
System which we’ve had and maintained for over 20 years and [ISO 14001:2015][59] Environmental
Management System which we added to our bow in 2019, to ensure quality assurance standards at every
stage of production. We also publish an [Environmental Statement][60] which you can view here. We’re
exceptionally proud of maintaining these over the years and the vigorous audits performed.

We have a Quality Management System that continuously improves our effectiveness in maintaining our
BS EN ISO 9001-defined requirements. We comply with all relevant standards and regulations and are
committed to delivering high-quality products and timely deliveries to ensure customer satisfaction.

> Our biggest achievements are maintaining ISO accreditations and introducing Standard Operating
> Procedures which improve and control our manufacturing processes.

Geoff Daniels Quality, Health & Safety Manager

> I can’t thank you enough for your care and attention to detail. I know you have all gone the extra
> mile for us, and I am extremely grateful. The quality of the parts has given our business the best
> possible start and will make a huge impact on the lives of the children who will be using our
> seating soon.

Chartered Engineer Medical Sector

## **Our quality assurance commitment**

At the helm of our quality initiatives is our dedicated Quality Manager. This role is pivotal in
embedding quality in every stage of the production process, ensuring that every product meets our
stringent requirements in the vast array of sectors we work with that require the upmost precision
from the defence and [aerospace][61] industry through to the healthcare and [industrial][62] sector.

Our commitment to quality assurance means that from the initial design phase through to final
production, robust quality control measures are in place. This meticulous approach guarantees that
we consistently deliver the highest quality products, reflecting our pledge to excellence.

## **Our customer charter**

Our customer charter serves as a cornerstone of our customer service philosophy, outlining the
fundamental values of reliability, trustworthiness, and quality that underpin every customer
interaction. This shows the high standards you can expect from Kewell Converters.

[View our Customer Charter][63]

> At Kewell Converters, quality isn't just a promise—it's a tradition. For over five decades, we've
> honed our precision and attention to detail, backed by an experienced team and robust processes.
> As a family-owned business, we pride ourselves on offering a personal, agile service, responding
> swiftly and effectively to the needs of our clients. This dedication to quality is what makes us a
> trusted partner in the supply chain, delivering complex foam solutions that not only meet but
> exceed expectations.

Nick Kewell Managing Director
[CNC router cutting case inserts. Batch manufacturing]

## **Innovative processes and technologies**

Innovation is at the heart of Kewell Converters, with continuous advancements being made to optimise
our processes. The implementation of [In Process Inspection][64] allows us to monitor and ensure
quality throughout every stage of production, minimising errors and maximising efficiency.
Additionally, the integration of ‘Maintain X’ software has significantly enhanced our productivity
by streamlining workflows, improving accuracy, and reducing waste. These pioneering technologies
testify to our commitment to excellence and sustainability.

[Learn about our Machine Capabilities][65]

## Bringing foam projects to life through CAD design

At Kewell Converters, every foam fabrication project begins as a blank canvas, primed for the
bespoke touch of our skilled CAD design team. Our trio of adept CAD CAM (Computer-Aided Design and
Computer-Aided Manufacturing) engineers view each project as a chance to craft a solution tailored
precisely to your needs.

Whether we’re pioneering concepts from scratch or refining simple sketches provided by our
customers, our team excels in transforming ideas into sophisticated designs. Specialising in foam—a
dynamic and lightweight material—our engineers bring unmatched expertise to every project. Foam’s
propensity to shift requires a nuanced design approach, often necessitating iterative revisions to
ensure perfection. This expertise sets our work apart, blending finesse with technical precision.

Understanding the importance of customer clarity, we produce both 2D and 3D visualisations using
SpaceClaim CAD modelling software. This critical step bridges the gap between concept and reality,
allowing our customers to envision the final product with crystal-clear acuity. Our commitment to
detail elevates us above the ordinary, embodying the hallmark of engineering excellence. To take
concepts to the next level, we create interactive digital designs that enable clients to manipulate
and explore the product, gaining a thorough understanding of what will be manufactured.

## Continuous improvement and staff development

We believe in the power of continuous improvement and recognise the crucial role of our staff in
achieving this and consistently producing products of the highest quality. Comprehensive training
programmes are integral to our strategy, equipping staff with the skills necessary to excel in their
roles. By setting clear objectives and targets for performance improvement, we maintain a culture of
excellence and adaptability.

## **Responding to customer needs**

Our customer-centric approach is characterised by a robust process for addressing quality concerns
promptly and professionally. We are dedicated to delivering swift resolutions, understanding that
responsiveness is key to customer satisfaction.

## Contact us

For all quality-related queries or to provide feedback, customers can email us [here][66]. Our
commitment to transparency and open communication ensures that every query is handled with care and
professionalism, reinforcing the trust our customers place in us.

Curious to learn more about our design and production process used for foam conversion projects? Get
in touch with us today to discuss how we can bring your ideas to life. Email
[enquiries@kewell-converters.co.uk][67]

# Foam mobility transfer step

## **Elevate mobility and safety with Kewell Converters’ premium foam solutions**

The importance of safety, independence, and quality of life for individuals with mobility challenges
can’t be overstated. In many environments such as healthcare, education, as well as in a residential
setting, the need to ensure secure and efficient wheelchair transfers is a priority. This blog
explores the challenges associated with wheelchair transfers, as well as a viable solution Kewell
Converters can offer using its robust medical foam products.

### **The challenge**

Ensuring the safety and independence of wheelchair users during transfers is an ongoing challenge.
For anyone reliant on a wheelchair, transferring to and from it, for instance, on to a toilet,
dining chair or bed, can be tricky, without the help of a carer. Wheelchair footplates, when
flipped to one side, leave a drop to the floor which may be difficult for a person to manoeuvre
safely.

Unsafe transfers can lead to falls, injuries, and a lack of self-sufficiency, impacting the overall
quality of life for individuals with mobility needs.

### **The solution**

One potential solution involves the use of foam mobility transfer steps which we’ve successfully
fabricated using specialist foam for many years for use in the [healthcare and medical sector][58].
Foam mobility transfer steps provide a stable and secure platform for wheelchair users,
significantly reducing the risk of falls and injuries during transfers. These steps enhance user
independence and versatility, allowing for varied applications across multiple settings.

We offer customisation of these steps in terms of shape, size, and design. This enables users to
choose options that match their personal preferences and environmental needs. Constructed from
medical-grade foams, these steps offer improved durability and non-slip properties, ensuring
long-term safety. By integrating foam mobility transfer steps into operations, organisations can
create supportive and inclusive environments that foster safety and independence for individuals
with mobility challenges.

### **Key features of foam mobility transfer steps**

#### **Lightweight and portable design**

One of the standout features of foam mobility transfer steps is their lightweight construction. This
makes them easy to carry and position around obstacles, a crucial consideration in dynamic
environments such as manufacturing facilities or crowded homes. The portability of these steps
ensures that they can be quickly deployed whenever and wherever needed, enhancing their utility and
convenience.

#### **Non-slip material**

Safety is a top priority when it comes to mobility aids. The use of medical-grade foams in the
construction of these transfer steps ensures a non-slip surface, providing secure footing during
transfers. This reduces the risk of slips and falls, which can lead to serious injuries. The
non-slip feature is especially important in wet or slick areas, such as bathrooms or kitchens, where
the risk of accidents is higher.

#### **Hygienic and easy to clean**

Maintaining hygiene is crucial in environments where mobility aids are used frequently. Foam
mobility transfer steps are designed to be easy to clean, with surfaces that can be wiped down with
disinfectant solutions. This ensures that the steps remain sanitary and safe for use, reducing the
risk of infections or cross-contamination. The ability to maintain high hygiene standards makes
these steps suitable for use in medical facilities, homes, and public spaces. Read more about our
[healthcare and hygiene foams][59].

### Conclusion

In summary, Kewell Converters’ premium medical foam solutions elevate both mobility and safety for
individuals with mobility challenges. By simplifying transfers with our innovative foam mobility
transfer steps, we ensure that safety, independence, and quality of life are prioritised in various
environments, including healthcare, education, and residential settings.

The challenge of ensuring safe and independent wheelchair transfers is significant, but our
specialised foam products provide a robust and reliable solution. Our foam mobility transfer steps
offer a stable and secure platform, reducing the risk of falls and injuries while enhancing user
independence. ]

Creating supportive and inclusive environments is more than just an operational goal; it’s a
commitment to fostering safety and independence for those with mobility challenges. By integrating
foam mobility transfer steps into your operations, you can make a meaningful difference.

# Foam tubing for the medical and healthcare sector

## Revolutionising medical support with foam tubing

At Kewell Converters, we have rich heritage in producing high-quality foam products that cater to a
variety of sectors for the [healthcare and medical industry][58]. This blog highlights our
innovative foam tubing solutions and their significant impact on medical support applications. We
truly believe our track record and dedication to enhancing the quality of life for individuals with
medical conditions sets us apart in the industry.

### The challenge

In the healthcare sector, medical support devices are crucial for patient rehabilitation and daily
living assistance. For people with neurological conditions like cerebral palsy or musculoskeletal
disorders such as arthritis, holding cutlery, or indeed any implement requiring a firm grip, can be
very difficult. Simple daily tasks, such as eating dinner, can become impossible without someone
else’s assistance.

However, these devices often lack the necessary comfort, durability, and adaptability to meet
varying patient needs. Traditional materials used in medical equipment can cause discomfort and
don’t always offer the flexibility required for effective rehabilitation. Production managers and
supply chain teams face the ongoing challenge of sourcing materials that not only meet regulatory
standards but also enhance the end-user experience.

### The solution

Kewell Converters addresses these challenges with our state-of-the-art foam tubing solutions,
particularly our unique use of Plastazote which had taken decades to finetune. Our medical foam
products offer unparalleled comfort, support, and versatility. The unique properties of Plastazote
make it an ideal choice for a wide range of medical applications, including grip enhancement on
everyday tools and critical support in medical devices.

## Key features of Plastazote foam tubing:
* **Comfort and support**: Plastazote provides a comfortable grip, essential for individuals with
limited hand strength
* **Versatility**: Can be used in various applications, from cutlery to medical devices
* **Durability**: Closed-cell foam tubing is light, non-absorbent, non-sticky, washable, and
dishwasher safe.
* **Customisable**: Supplied in one-metre lengths and can be cut to size, making it easy to tailor
to specific needs

This product is highly sought after by occupational therapists who aim to improve daily living for
their clients. The closed-cell foam tubing is available in various sizes to provide a built-up
handle for easier gripping (e.g., cutlery, pens). It’s lightweight, non-absorbent, and can be washed
or placed in a dishwasher, ensuring hygiene and ease of use.

### Versatile applications in healthcare

Many of the foams specified by our customers need to be in skin contact and must be MRI, CT, and
X-Ray lucent, so they can be deployed in splint and support applications we manufacture. Some
specific applications include:

### Prosthetics

Our [Azote][59] foams are often specified for prosthetic applications due to their very low mass and
wide range of available densities, making them suitable for numerous podiatric applications,
including Plantar Fasciitis, Pes Planus, and Pes Cavus.

### Joint and spinal supports

Plastazote and other foams are used in “moulding to the body” applications, such as the manufacture
of joint supports, spinal supports, and immobilising orthoses.

### Hydrotherapy equipment

The hydrophobic and flexible nature of our foams makes them ideal for manufacturing hydrotherapy
equipment.

Our commitment to innovation means we continuously explore new applications and improvements to our
existing products, ensuring that we meet the ever-evolving and essential needs of the healthcare
sector.

# Cases and custom foam inserts

## **How foam inserts enhanced product protection for a leading visual merchandising company**

### **Background**

In the fast-paced world of visual merchandising, precision and attention to detail are paramount.
Our client, a highly regarded business with over two decades of experience, faced an urgent
challenge. Tasked with delivering 250 bespoke packaging units for a high-profile product launch,
they needed a manufacturer who could deliver quickly and without compromising on quality.

### **The challenge**

The client required custom foam inserts that would:
* **Protect the product:** Ensuring the delicate items remained intact during transport
* **Provide a premium presentation:** Enhancing the product’s appeal with a high-quality finish
* **Offer bespoke design and customisation:** Tailored to fit perfectly within the packaging units

Given the tight lead times and high expectations, finding the right partner was crucial.

### **The solution**

Kewell Converters stepped up to the challenge, leveraging their expertise in protective foam
solutions. Within two weeks of the initial contact, two foam insert prototypes were designed and
presented to the client. The selected materials included:
* **Azote Foam:** Known for its protective and aesthetic qualities
* **Closed Cell Polyethylene Foam:** Chosen in black to achieve a premium look

### **Key features**
* **Protective foam:** Ensured the product remained secure and undamaged
* **Bespoke design:** Customised to fit the client’s specific requirements
* **High-quality finish:** Enhanced the product’s presentation, creating a ‘wow’ moment for the
audience

### **The results**

The collaboration led to flawless execution and impeccable design, meeting the client’s high
standards. The quick turnaround, coupled with efficient and professional service, ensured the
project’s success.

The client expressed their immense satisfaction with the project, stating:

*“We specialise in the difficult and sometimes impossible – whether this is down to the incredibly
tight lead times, or just the unusual nature of the enquiry. When we were tasked with creating
bespoke packaging units for a high-end, product launch, we looked to outsource the custom foam
parts. After contacting several foam converters to help us out, Kewell Converters were the only
company to be unfazed by our request, the quantity required and the timescales. Following our first
face-to-face meeting, it was clear they were the perfect partner. The whole team were responsive and
wasted no time getting started. Each part we received was to the same high-quality finish as the
first, and exactly as expected. The project was a big success and very well received by the client
and recipients.”*

## **Why choose Kewell Converters for custom foam inserts?**

Kewell Converters design and manufacture bespoke foam inserts for numerous industries, also sourcing
and supplying cases. We collaborate with premium case manufacturers to offer cost-efficient and
practical casing solutions for Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs). Some of the renowned brands

Working with leading UK visual merchandising companies, we ensure that quality is paramount. Our

# Luxury sustainable fashion

## **Revolutionising luxury sustainable fashion with Kewell Converters’ foam inserts**** **

### **Using innovative foam materials to reshape the fashion industry**

#### **Background**

In an era where environmental consciousness and sustainability are paramount, Stitchsmith London
stands out as a trailblazer in the fashion industry. Based in London, this luxury sustainable
fashion brand has developed the world’s first truly customisable clutch bag. The innovation lies in
its ability to be re-covered in any fabric, enabling customers to personalise it repeatedly. This
unique approach not only reduces waste but also encourages upcycling of materials already owned by
the user.

### **The brief**

Stitchsmith London sought a reliable partner to join their sustainable supply chain—one that could
meet their high-quality standards for foam inserts while minimising environmental impact. They
approached Kewell Converters with a specific need for foam inserts that wouldn’t only form part of
the clutch bag’s structure but also align with their [sustainability][58] ethos. The foam had to be
versatile enough to allow the clutch to be re-covered by the customer with new or upcycled fabric,
thus making each bag a long-lasting, multi-functional accessory.

### **The solution**

Kewell Converters rose to the challenge by providing polyethylene [foam inserts][59] with adhesive
backing. This solution met all of Stitchsmith London’s requirements:
* **High quality**: The [polyethylene foam][60] adds a soft touch and premium luxury feel, essential
for a high-end fashion accessory
* **Versatility**: The foam’s adhesive backing enables easy re-covering with various fabrics,
whether new or upcycled, making it a versatile component of the clutch
* **Sustainability**: The use of polyethylene foam aligns with Stitchsmith’s commitment to reducing
waste and minimising environmental impact during production

The foam insert’s ability to stick to any fabric ensures that customers can effortlessly personalise
their clutch, making it an exciting and sustainable product. This collaboration showcases the
versatility of polyethylene foam, proving its efficacy in diverse applications.

## **Choosing the right manufacturing partner to achieve your sustainability goals**

The partnership between Stitchsmith London and Kewell Converters exemplifies how innovative
materials and sustainable practices can reshape the fashion industry. By integrating high-quality,
versatile, and [eco-friendly foam][61] inserts into their customisable clutch bags, Stitchsmith has
set a new standard for luxury sustainable fashion.

Watch the [Stitchsmith Clutch][62] video to learn more about this groundbreaking project and how you
can be a part of this sustainable fashion revolution.

### **The background**

Catherine de Crèvecoeur is a premium jewellery label from Kent, specializing in unique handcrafted
statement pieces using ethically sourced leather materials. The brand’s meticulous focus on details
guarantees exquisite beauty and superior quality in every finished product.

### **The problem**

While the company’s designs change with each season, they were limited in their production
capabilities to cope with the scale at which the business was expanding. With intricate design
shapes, they needed to understand the elements that could be utilised to maximise cutting their
materials. Since launching the business, the jewellery business had relied on a number of small mini
press machines for cutting leather, which was labour-intensive and not efficient.

“We just kept getting bigger machines, but were restricted with the shapes and types of leather.”
Catherine de Crèvecoeur

As the business expanded, they no longer had the in-house capabilities and they couldn’t ramp up
production when required so they sought expert help within the manufacturing sector.

### **The solution**

Kewell Converters provided consultancy and technical advice on tooling design and production and
provided subcontract manufacturing using the latest die press-making tools.

One of the first services that Kewell Converters provided was to help the jewellery business get
accustomed to press-making tools to stay in sync with their designs so they put them in touch with
their trusted toolmaker. But Catherine de Crèvecoeur soon realized that to press the shapes out of
the leather, they needed more than just a new press machine. And after careful consideration and
evaluation, they realised that owning, working, and maintaining these powerful and expensive cutting
machines required expertise that goes beyond what [Catherine de Crèvecoeur][58] initially had in
mind.

Kewell Converters got straight to work and provided in-depth testing and trials before the use of
their production facilities. They gave advice on what’s possible in terms of tooling design to make
sure that the tools could cut the products. In addition, they upskilled the team to use the dirt and
press machines with confidence, which helped improve production and meet customer demand.

### **Precision cutting with our state-of-the-art die-cutting process**

Thanks to our advanced die-cutting process, we were able to offer precision cutting. This is
specifically designed for soft and semi-rigid materials and our cutting-edge machinery ensures
unparalleled speed, accuracy, and material efficiency, so it was perfect for the job in hand.

Our versatile travelling head cutting press machines are ideal for handling sheet material, long
lays, or even material straight from the roll. With a motorized cutting head that effortlessly moves
within the press frame, our skilled operators manually position the die for optimal results. No job
is too big, as our machines can handle materials up from 1.5 to 2 meters wide and are easily fed
through the rear of the press.

When it comes to tooling, there are three main types to suit a range of needs. Wood forme, strip
steel, or forged steel. Our wood forme features a cutting blade set in a sturdy plywood backer,
while our strip steel uses a heavier gauge steel that is bent to the required shape. For the most
demanding applications, our forged steel tooling delivers unparalleled precision, making it ideal
for long runs and harder materials. The Flexible Travelling Head Cutting Press (rarely achieved by
other press styles and is the natural progression if a swing arm press is too small or limited for
an application was used for Catherine de Crèvecoeur.

### **The results**

Thanks to Kewell Converters, the jewellery business achieved a tenfold increase in production
capacity by improving efficiency. Previously, their bracelets’ cutting process was inefficient and
resulted in high reject rates and loss of raw materials. However, with Kewell Converter’s expert
guidance and facilities, they achieved better yield, less waste, and cost savings. This allowed the
business to design and produce cost-effective, fashionable, and customized products with better
quality control. As a result, they became more responsive and proactive to the market’s changing
demands, giving them a competitive edge.

“The quality is very good. And it’s reliable. It helps everything to run smoothly.” Catherine de
Crèvecoeur

The jewellery businesses can now design and produce cost-effective products with a high degree of
fashion and customization thanks to the high-quality machines in the factory at Kewell Converters.
This skill set has enabled them to be more reactive and proactive with their designs, changing their
stock and products depending on the season or market trends.

“We could immediately see the difference in quality. We achieved a cleaner cut and could produce a
more versatile product range.” Catherine de Crèvecoeur

At Kewell Converters, we offer consultancy and subcontract manufacturing services to businesses.
Subcontract manufacturing allows you to scale up production without making a large capital
investment. You can turn it on and off as needed, making it a flexible option. We helped Catherine
de Crèvecoeur maximize their yield and achieve the highest quality products while reducing waste and
cost. Our relationship with raw material manufacturers also allowed them to procure premium
materials at competitive prices.

We take pride in being a reliable partner for businesses looking to drive efficiency in their
production processes. Catherine de Crèvecoeur leveraged our expertise to produce cost-efficient
custom designs at scale. From consultancy to subcontract manufacturing, our comprehensive services
allow businesses to remain responsive and proactive in changing stock and product lines. Let us help
you streamline your production processes too.

“Kewell Converters are experts in everything they do. They allowed us to see how far we could take
the business. Catherine de Crèvecoeur

Working with Kewell Converters has indeed provided Catherine de Crèvecoeur with a competitive edge
in the market.

“As a small business being able to access and use Kewell Converters, it’s made a big difference.
It’s been a game changer.” Catherine de Crèvecoeur

# Bespoke foam stools

## **Elevate exhibitions with custom foam solutions: How Kewell Converters partnered with the
## National Maritime Museum**

### **The problem**

The National Maritime Museum faced a specific challenge with their new exhibition aimed at children.
They needed seating that wasn’t only functional but also engaging and visually appealing to young
visitors. The stools had to be durable enough to withstand frequent use while being comfortable and
inviting for children. Additionally, the museum required the stools to blend seamlessly with the
exhibition’s aesthetic, adding a pop of[ colour][58] and creativity to the space.

### **The solution**

Kewell Converters approached this challenge by leveraging extensive expertise in foam products. We
collaborated closely with the museum’s design team to understand the specific requirements and
constraints, having worked with many of our clients in-house design teams. We went through the
following process:

#### **Design consultation**

Kewell Converters engaged in detailed discussions with the museum’s designers to gather insights
into the exhibition’s theme, colour scheme, and functional needs

#### **Material selection**

The team selected high-quality, child-friendly foam materials using Plastazote and Evazote, from the
Zotefoams Azote range of materials that were durable, easy to clean, and safe for children

#### **Custom design**

Kewell Converters designed unique stool shapes and sizes that would be both comfortable and visually
appealing. The designs led by our CAD design team included vibrant colours and playful shapes to
attract children’s attention.

#### **Manufacturing**

Once the designs were approved, Kewell Converters manufactured the stools with precision ready for
the exhibition launch.

### **Results**

This collaboration yielded outstanding results. The foam stools enhanced the overall experience for
young visitors. The colourful and uniquely designed stools attracted children, encouraging them to
participate in research tasks and interact more deeply with the exhibition

The success of this project reinforced Kewell Converters’ reputation as a reliable and innovative
foam partner. We are now the preferred and approved foam supplier for many museums, theatres, film
and TV production companies including V&A Museum, Natural History Museum, Oxford University Museum
of Natural History, Royal National Theatre, Royal Museums Greenwich, The National Gallery, and the
National Archives, The National Library of Wales, Victoria & Albert Museum and Kilmartin Museum.

### ** ****A trusted foam supplier for the leisure sector**

This case study demonstrates our capability to deliver bespoke solutions that meet very specific
client needs.

With a proven track record of delivering innovative and high-quality foam products, Kewell
Converters is well-positioned to continue supporting museums and other organisations in the leisure
industry create engaging and functional spaces.

Ready to elevate your next project with custom foam solutions? View our [case studies][59] to learn
more and discover our vast [machine capabilities][60].

# Playground equipment

## LARGE BALL SKILLS PANEL & VELCRO TARGET SET

Another innovative result of our collaboration with Playforce, a company based in Melksham,
Wiltshire, who create imaginative play areas for young children at playgroups, nurseries and primary
schools, both indoors and outdoors.

Play is an important part of learning, social development and encouraging physical skills and
movement.

These foam targets, produced by Kewell, are made in segments so can be arranged in many formations
to suit whatever’s going on. They’re safe to use, versatile, lightweight and easy to store. They’re
also durable and easy to keep clean. Assembly is simple and fun. Even a child could do it – which
could be part of the whole learning experience.

Throwing balls at the targets will help to develop hand-eye coordination and muscular strength. For
budding cricketers, we also make foam wickets to go against a wall.

With the added benefit of outdoor Velcro strips on this large ball skills panel, children can create
their own targets and move them around each day to vary the challenge and create new games. We
helped bring the concept and vison of our client into a practical design and a real foam products
into the market place and schools across the UK. These are fabricated and manufactured from EVA
FOAM – a closed cell (non-porous) durable plastic foam material made of EVA (Ethylene Vinyl Acetate)
and PE (Polyethylene) resin. Traditional EVA foam material is mainly used for shoe insoles, sport
goods, mats for karate, taekwondo, yoga, martial art exercises, and machinery cushion.

Aside:-

2012 was a golden year for English sport, uniting the nation in support and appreciation of our
athletes and their achievements. But in the wake of the Games, there has been concern among
headteachers about future generations of children missing out on a sustainable, meaningful Olympic
legacy.

Only half of headteachers and 27% of the children we asked still talk about the Games, and sports
provision in schools must be held accountable for this. Almost 100% of the headteachers
we [surveyed ][58]believed the Games had a positive impact on their school, but their legacy is
compromised by demands of timetables and budgeting.

The recent £300m investment in primary school PE is a welcome reinforcement of the national appeal
for improved equipment and specialist coaching. However this scheme was enabled by the dismantling
of existing, successful support structures and it is this inconsistency which headteachers must
overcome when deciding how to allocate the extra funding.

To succeed as a sustainable and long-term initiative, the funding can be divided between investments
in high-quality playground equipment, and specialist training for teachers. As concluded in an
Ofsted report earlier this year, the majority of school PE lessons lack sufficient strenuous,
physical activity and attributed this shortcoming to a lack of confidence among teachers.

Teachers are already under immense pressure from the Labour Party’s proposal for longer school days,
with stress-related absence up by 50% in local authorities across England. However the extra funding
can be used to relieve some of this pressure by providing further support and coaching, reinforcing
PE as a supplement, not an interruption, to learning.

No longer the domain of star jumps and relay races, new and innovative equipment and resources can

# Playforce transforms children’s playtime with Kewell Converters’ dynamic foam solutions

## **Creating 3D foam shapes for the leisure industry**

Playforce, a leader in creating play environments for children in the [leisure][58] industry, faced
the challenge of designing versatile and engaging play structures that aligned with school
curriculums in the UK. Partnering with Kewell Converters, Playforce implemented the innovative
modular system Poddely, using durable and vibrant [3D foam shapes][59] for the leisure industry.
This collaboration resulted in a significant enhancement to imaginative play, seamlessly integrating
with educational frameworks and providing a sustainable, safe environment for children through the
innovative use of foam.

#### **Introduction**

Playforce has been supplying creative play environments throughout the UK for over 15 years. Based
in Melksham, Wiltshire, Playforce has leveraged Kewell Converters’ expertise in foam products and 3D
foam shapes to design interactive installations for schools, nurseries, and playgroups.

#### **The problem**

Despite Playforce’s success, they faced a challenge common to many educational play
providers—developing play structures that remained both engaging and adaptable while meeting the
diverse demands of the curriculum. Recognising the need for a solution that would allow children to
explore creativity safely and with versatility, Playforce turned to Kewell Converters.

#### **The solution**

In collaboration with education practitioners, designers, and, most crucially, the children
themselves, Playforce developed Poddely, an innovative modular system. Kewell Converters played a
pivotal role in this development by supplying the foam components crafted from their
high-performance, impact-absorbing materials. These foams, available in bright, eye-catching
colours, not only enhance the visual appeal but also ensure durability and safety.

Poddely’s design allows for the creation of cubes, prisms, and flat surfaces through interlocking
tiles, providing endless possibilities for imaginative play. The foam used is weather-resistant and
retains its structural integrity, making it ideal for both indoor and outdoor environments.

#### **Results**

The introduction of Poddely revolutionised Playforce’s offerings. Children now have the freedom to
transform the modular foam structures into castles, spacecraft, pirate ships, or fairy palaces,
limited only by their imagination. This adaptability not only enhances playtime but also aligns
perfectly with the Early Years, KS1, and KS2 curriculum, making it an invaluable educational asset.

Our foam components have proven to be exceptional in their performance, offering optimal cushioning
and impact absorption, which are critical for safe play. The versatility of the foam, with its
ability to laminate with various [materials][60] and adhere to diverse surfaces, sets it apart in
the market. The strategic use of [colour][61] further boosts engagement, encouraging learning and
playful behaviour among children.

### **Inspiring the next generation of thinkers and creators**

The partnership between Kewell Converters and Playforce shows the power of innovative thinking and
collaboration in addressing the challenges of modern play environments. Together, we’ve created a
product that not only meets educational needs but also inspires the next generation of thinkers and
creators.

For more information on how Kewell Converters can help transform your ideas into impactful solutions
please email our expert team [here][62] and they would be delighted to assist.

# Exquisite bespoke jewellery insert

## Combining sustainability and luxury craftsmanship

Experience the breath-taking artistry of Irene & Jenny as they transform your beloved heirloom
jewellery into one-of-a-kind masterpieces designed to last for generations. This mother-daughter
duo, based in Kent, has built their business on passion, history, and sustainability. Each piece
they create has a story to tell; a diamond from a mother’s wedding ring, a sapphire to celebrate the
birth of a child, or a cluster of rubies from a romantic adventure abroad. They encapsulate
generations of memories in a single, stunning masterpiece.

When the founder of the business approached Kewell Converters to create a bespoke jewellery insert
for a high-value, precious bracelet, the results were truly extraordinary.

### **The challenge**

Crafting the perfect accompaniment for this exquisite bracelet was no small feat. Kewell Converters
needed to carefully select a sustainable, recycled foam grade and source matching-coloured leather
to compliment a beautiful clamshell-shaped box with a custom insert. The goal was to securely hold
and showcase the jewellery while ensuring durability and longevity.

### **The solution**

Under the leadership of Marcos Kewell and his team of skilled professionals, they employed
eco-friendly materials, including a 30% recycled foam called [Ecozote][58], manufactured by
[Zotefoams][59]. The size and orientation of the insert were thoughtfully considered to create an
impressive presentation when opened.

The project began with the design team, who expertly translated the business founder’s vision into
proposals. The Cad department led by John and his team then refined the font size, logo style, and
experimented with laser engraving parameters to achieve the desired visual impact. A series of tests
were conducted to ensure optimal marking and presentation. With the design finalised, Kewell
Converters moved on to pre-production and full-scale production, including cutting trials to achieve
the perfect fit. To compliment the bespoke insert, Kewell Converters sourced premium leather from
Italy, leveraging their five decades of experience working with top manufacturers worldwide. Several
samples were obtained and meticulously colour-matched, guaranteeing a flawless integration with the
final product. Laser etching and the client’s personalised logo added an extra touch of
individuality and luxury to the final product.

### **The results**

Upon completion, Anita Brightley-Hodges expressed her satisfaction, stating, “The customer was
absolutely thrilled with the final product and described it as stunning work. Kewell Converters are
an exceptional business, and they were the only choice to align with our brand values. We tell
stories and need to convey empathy, so every aspect of the material and packaging must be part of
the narrative, and they exceeded our expectations.”

Marcos Kewell remarked, “This was a wonderful and truly special project to be a part of. We loved
being involved and were thrilled with the end result and what my team managed to create. Working in
the luxury sector always presents challenges, but achieving aesthetic perfection is always our
goal.”

The collaboration between Irene & Jenny and Kewell Converters resulted in an exceptional and

# Dunlop oil and marine, selflote

## **Overcoming challenges in marine buoyancy with specialist foams**

Dunlop oil and marine (DOM), part of Continental AG, is recognised as the leading supplier of
offshore loading hoses to all major oil, gas and petrochemical companies worldwide. As a pioneer in
offshore oil hose technology, they faced significant challenges in ensuring the durability and
reliability of their floating hose products, Selflote and Saflote. They turned to Zotefoams who
engaged Kewell Converters to collaborate on the manufacture of advanced foam solutions. Selflote
and Saflote required state of the art foam solutions that provided exceptional mechanical and
chemical properties suitable for harsh marine environments. The collaboration resulted in the
development of the world’s first integrally floated offshore oil hose, setting a new industry
standard for flexibility, strength, and resistance to tough conditions.

### **The problem**

DOM faced a significant challenge in looking for specialist manufactured foams for marine buoyancy,
particularly for ship-to-shore pipelines. The marine environment, characterised by salt water,
chemical exposure, and physical stress, demanded materials that could withstand these conditions
while maintaining performance integrity. Traditional materials failed to provide the necessary
combination of low mass, high flexibility, and durability, leading to frequent maintenance issues
and operational inefficiencies.

### **The solution**

DOM consulted with Zotefoams who collaborated with Kewell Converters to create bespoke designs for
the floating hoses. After in-depth consultations, we supplied high density foams using [Azote][58]
product, Plastazote, which offered the perfect blend of characteristics required for marine buoyancy
applications including:
* **Mechanical strength**: These foams manufactured by Zotefoams and then fabricated by Kewell
Converters, provided exceptional durability and energy absorption, essential for withstanding
physical stress.
* **Low mass and high flexibility**: The properties in the foams ensured the products could perform
efficiently in dynamic marine environments.
* **Chemical resistance**: The inherent hydrophobic nature and inertness of the foams made them
resistant to salt water and chemical degradation.
* **Flame retardancy**: This was crucial for safety in offshore installations.

### **Results**

The partnership between Zotefoams and Kewell Converters led to remarkable outcomes, establishing a
new benchmark in the marine industry. The Selflote offshore oil hose product became the industry
standard which others are compared, thanks to its unique design and superior performance. The
innovative use of specialist foams and complex conversion of these foams resulted in products that
offer unmatched performance, durability, and reliability even in the harshest marine environments
including:
* **Proven design**: The Selflote hose demonstrated exceptional reliability and performance in the
most exposed offshore installations
* **Highly flexible**: Capable of withstanding dynamic marine conditions
* **Specialised fitting design**: Enhancing ease of installation and maintenance
* **Floatation bonding system**: Resisting sea water ingress and maintaining performance integrity

### **Setting a new standard in marine buoyancy**

This unique and complex project not only addressed the critical challenges faced by DOM but also set
new industry standards for marine buoyancy solutions.

The ongoing collaboration promises to drive more innovations, ensuring Selflote remains at the
forefront of the offshore oil and gas industry.

# Masuri cricket helmets

## **Masuri and Kewell Converters: Redefining safety standards in cricket helmets**

### **Enhancing safety and performance through innovative foam solutions**

Masuri, a leading manufacturer of cricket helmets, faced the challenge of enhancing helmet safety
and performance to meet stringent industry standards. Partnering with Kewell Converters, we
developed foam components that significantly improved the durability and functionality of their
Vision Series helmets. This collaboration resulted in helmets that not only met but exceeded
existing safety standards, helping solidify Masuri’s position as a market leader.

### **Introduction**

[Masuri][58], based near Winchester, is renowned for producing the highest quality cricket helmets
used by professional teams worldwide. Known for their lightweight design and unmatched comfort,
Masuri helmets are meticulously crafted to ensure maximum safety for cricket players. The company
invests heavily in research and development to explore innovative technologies, resulting in
pioneering patents such as Active Peak Tech and Eyeline Grille. The Vision Series, strengthened by
the Halo Reinforcement system, exemplifies Masuri’s commitment to excellence.

### **The problem**

The International Cricket Council identified the need for further improvements in helmet safety,
prompting Masuri to innovate. To achieve these stringent specifications, Masuri needed to develop
advanced foam components that would enhance the durability and functionality of their helmets. This
required substantial investment in research and development and collaboration with experts in
material technology.

### **The foam solution**

As specialists in the development and conversion of foam components, we were involved from the early
stages of research and development, working closely with John Hardy, the former English cricketer.
This collaboration led to the creation of trial foam components and prototypes tailored to the new
Masuri Cricket Helmets.

The process involved numerous site meetings where carefully selected foam [materials][59] were
reviewed and several iterations of designs and end parts were tested. We played a crucial role in
finalising the foam polymer, grade, colour, and finish for production. Our expertise ensured that
the final product met Masuri’s high standards for safety and performance.

### **Setting new standards**

The collaboration between Masuri and Kewell Converters culminated in the development of the Masuri
Vision Series helmets, which set new standards in the competitive cricket helmet market. The
innovative design incorporated an articulated peak (Active Peak Tech) and a reinforced Eyeline
Grille, effectively deflecting balls away from the player’s face. These features not only met the
existing safety standards but exceeded them, establishing a new benchmark for cricket helmet safety.

The Vision Series received widespread acclaim for its superior safety and comfort. Masuri’s
partnership with us enabled them to deliver a product that combined cutting-edge technology with
practical design, ensuring the highest level of protection for players.

### **A manufacturing partnership that drove innovation**

The successful collaboration between Masuri and Kewell Converters highlights the importance of
manufacturing partnerships in driving innovation and achieving industry-leading results. By
leveraging our expertise in foam technology, Masuri were able to overcome significant challenges and
deliver a product that redefined safety standards in cricket helmets.

# Levi’s Live Unbuttoned Campaign with Kewell Converters

# Overcoming Artistic Challenges with High-Performance Foams

### **Creative foam solutions: bringing iconic art to life for Levi’s Live Unbuttoned Campaign**

Levi Jeans, as part of their Live Unbuttoned 501 campaign in London in 2008, wanted to create a
captivating multimedia outdoor wall poster inspired by The Great Wave at Kanagawa. They partnered
with Kewell Converters, who used Plastazote® high-performance foams to fabricate intricate designs.

### **Introduction**

Levi Jeans, a global leader in the denim industry, aimed to make a bold statement with their Live
Unbuttoned 501 campaign in London. The campaign sought to engage the urban audience through creative
and visually striking advertisements. They decided to create a large-scale multimedia outdoor wall
poster inspired by Katsushika Hokusai’s famous artwork, The Great Wave at Kanagawa. To bring this
artistic vision to life, they turned to Kewell Converters, tasking us with developing an intricate
design which used Azote foam to create the precise contours on top of the waves.

### **The Problem**

The advertising agency faced a significant challenge—they needed to fabricate the complex design of
the foam on top of the waves using actual foam. Additionally, traditional blue Levi jeans were to
represent the sea, forming eight-foot-high denim waves, all secured onto a foam backing. The posters
were destined for high-traffic locations in London, including Chalk Farm Road, Camden, Wardour
Street, Soho, and Shoreditch High Street. The intricate nature of the design required a material
that could be easily manipulated while maintaining structural integrity and aesthetic appeal, with
strict [quality assurance][58] to ensure durability in high-visibility settings.

### **The Solution**

Kewell Converters identified Plastazote® high-performance foams as the ideal material for this
project due to their versatility and ease of manipulation. [Zotefoams][59], the world’s leading
manufacturer of polyolefin block foams, provided the Plastazote®, Evazote®, and Supazote® brands,
collectively known as ‘Azote®’ foams. These foams are characterised by their lightweight, consistent
cell size, depth of colour, and lack of in-built stresses, making them perfect for artistic
applications.

The key features of Azote® foams include:
* **Manipulability**: The foams could be cut, carved, welded, laminated, and manipulated with ease
* **Thermoforming capability**: They could be easily thermoformed at relatively low temperatures,
suitable for creating complex shapes
* **Lightweight and durable**: Despite their lightweight nature, the foams offered outstanding
physical performance characteristics

By leveraging these properties, Kewell Converters sculpted the intricate foam designs representing
the crest of the waves. They used traditional blue Levi jeans to depict the sea, creating
eight-foot-high denim waves secured onto the foam backing. The process involved cutting, carving,
and thermoforming the foam to match the artistic vision accurately.

### **Results**

The collaboration resulted in a series of visually stunning and unique campaign posters for Levi’s
Live Unbuttoned 501 campaign. The posters gained significant attention and admiration from passersby
and the media alike. Placed in prime locations in London, the posters left a lasting impression on
passers by, perfectly capturing the essence of the campaign.

### **Results included:**
* **Increased footfall**: The eye-catching design drew more foot traffic to the locations where the
posters were displayed
* **Media coverage**: The innovative use of foam and denim garnered significant media attention,
further amplifying the campaign’s reach
* **Brand engagement**: The unique and artistic approach resonated with the audience, enhancing
brand engagement and recall.

### **Conclusion**

The successful partnership between Levi Jeans and Kewell Converters demonstrates the power of
combining artistic vision with innovative foam [materials][60]. By leveraging the unique properties
of Plastazote® foams, Kewell Converters overcame the challenge of fabricating intricate designs,
resulting in a set of campaign posters that captivated the audience.

Read more of our customer case studies including [Masuri and Kewell Converters: Redefining safety
standards in cricket helmets][61]** and **[From concept to retail reality: creating foam parts for
the fashion and retail industry][62].

create unforgettable campaigns for your business.

# From concept to retail reality: creating foam parts for the fashion and retail industry

### **How Kewell Converters’ high-performance closed cell foam parts enabled a seamless design for a
### sustainable fashion brand**

**Background**

A new retail client Freitag specialising in upcycled bags approached Kewell Converters with an
ambitious project. They needed foam parts to form part of the design for a new line of recycled bags
made from a material containing recycled PET bottles in addition to discarded truck tarps and
reflectors. Kewell Converters were tasked with manufacturing prototypes and fulfilling the order
for this sustainable brand.

**Challenge**

The foam needed to integrate seamlessly into this sustainable design, as well as provide cushioning
and comfort for the end user as a padded laptop compartment. The challenge was significant. Kewell
Converters had to produce many customized foam parts within a 12-week timeframe.

On top of timing constraints, foam, although versatile, can be unpredictable, and issues such as
blowholes can arise. But Kewell Converters are highly skilled. Through stringent quality control
measures, we have the expertise and know-how to work with a vast range of complex materials.

**Solution**

After initial discussions with foam manufacturer [Zotefoams][58], Kewell Converters selected Zotek
NB50 to make the foam parts. This is a high performance closed cell, cross-linked Nylon foam and
would integrate perfectly with a nylon bag for a retail brand to achieve consistency in the base
product.

Kewell Converters had some of the required material in stock, and got straight to work with the
prototypes. Following approval of these, the engineering team progressed production and began
fulfilling this order using the Hawkes NC40 die cutting press.

**Results**

The project was executed flawlessly, with zero rejected products and timely delivery. Impressed with
the meticulous attention to detail and transparent communication, the client has subsequently
selected Kewell Converters as their preferred partner for another project as well as recommending to
another company. By overcoming unique challenges with expertise and clear communication, Kewell
Converters has proven to be a trustworthy and skilled partner for complex foam projects.

For more information on how Kewell Converters can support your retail or manufacturing needs with
versatile foam solutions, visit [enquiries@kewell-converters.co.uk][59]

including a [luxury sustainable fashion brand][60] and creating an [exquisite bespoke jewellery
insert][61].

# Precision under pressure: custom foam solutions for MOD applications

### **Delivering defence-grade foam parts **

### **Background**

At Kewell Converters, we’re proud to be recognised as one of the UK’s leading foam converters,
delivering bespoke foam solutions across a wide range of industries, from automotive and aerospace
to defence and military packaging. Our specialist team has decades of experience in providing
high-quality, precision-engineered foam parts that meet even the most complex requirements.

Recently, we were approached by an established supplier to navies across the globe—to help develop a
highly specialised product for the Ministry of Defence (MoD). The task? To create a removable
capture container for active defence hardware, which included a metal panel cover with a
precision-cut foam insert bonded on the underside to capture the required parts during live service
—an uncommon and technically demanding combination that required meticulous planning, sourcing, and
production.

### **The challenge**

This wasn’t the first time we had worked on [defence][58]-related projects, but this request stood
out due to the rare requirement of bonding foam parts to a metal component. While we had completed
similar projects in the past, the combination of materials, compliance demands, and the scale of the
job presented a unique challenge.

Several factors were non-negotiable:
* Use of defence-approved materials, including military grade foam
* Full traceability across the supply chain
* Consistent supply on a scheduled basis
* A scalable, repeatable process that could be rolled out again as required
* Above all, absolute confidence in the foam’s performance and protective capabilities

Kewell Converter’s ability to design and manufacture custom-made MoD-approved foam packaging made us
a natural choice for the project. Take a further look at our [blog][59] to learn more about our
proud legacy with the defence and military industry.

### **The solution**

Led by [Geoff][60] and [Neil][61] from our manufacturing team, the project began with detailed
product testing to ensure that the foam met the MoD’s strict safety and performance requirements.
This involved submitting extensive documentation and [quality assurance][62] paperwork—a process
that normally takes a few days but extended over several months due to the complexity of the supply
chain.

The raw materials specified by the customer were LD45 Plastazote for the foam insert and aluminum
for the cover panel. [Plastazote][63] is a high-quality material known for its strength, durability,
and protective properties. It was required to meet military specification Def Stan 81-116, Grade C,
Type QX. The cover panel was made from an Aluminium alloy, cut to include access features, and
anodized to a military specification, before being primed and painted in NATO Green (BS381C), but
only on one surface.

This specialised military-grade parts needed to be sourced, tested, and approved before any
manufacturing could commence.

Kewell Converters managed four separate suppliers for the project, sourcing the metal, paint, and
foam locally, ensuring every element met MoD standards. With a concept drawing already supplied, our
in-house design team created precision cutting programmes and issued a works order to the factory
floor.

The production process was multi-stage and highly detailed involving:
* Foam splitting and laminating
* Use of our adhesive machine
* Die stamping with our press machine
* Precision [CNC routing][64] to ensure exact dimensions
* Final assembly of foam onto the metal lids

Each part required a full week of combined labour, and the initial batch included over 100 units. In
the following month, we successfully ramped up production meeting the customer’s exact
specifications and schedule.

### **The results**

From testing and compliance through to fabrication and delivery, the project ran smoothly thanks to
the careful coordination and expertise of [our team][65]. The customer was extremely pleased with
the quality and repeatability of the final product. Most importantly, the components provided robust
product protection and met all MoD requirements.

This project is a prime example of how Kewell Converters combines technical know-how, specialist
sourcing, and precise foam fabrication to deliver complex, high-value solutions for the defence
sector. Whether it’s military foam solutions, custom foam defence components, or repeatable foam
conversion processes, we deliver reliability and results at every stage.

### **Looking for defence-grade foam expertise you can rely on?**

Whether you need custom-made MoD-approved foam packaging, military grade foam, or repeatable,
high-spec foam solutions for defence and aerospace applications, Kewell Converters has the
experience and capability to deliver. From concept to production, we specialise in
precision-engineered foam parts that meet the most demanding standards.

# Kewell Converters and Rega RP8 Turntable Partnership: Revolutionising Vinyl Playback with
# Precision Foam Engineering

### **Engineering Innovation: The Role of Precision Foam in Rega’s Vinyl Revolution**

## **Introduction**

[Rega][58], a world-renowned audio equipment manufacturer, faced the challenge of creating a
state-of-the-art turntable to meet the resurgent demand for vinyl records. Kewell Converters
provided the specialised acoustic foam required for the Rega RP8 Turntable, enhancing its design and
functionality. The collaboration resulted in a turntable that combines low mass with high rigidity,
offering unparalleled sound quality and earning accolades from top designers Sir Jony Ive and Marc
Newson.

### **The Problem**

The recent vinyl revival presented both an opportunity and a challenge for Rega. In 2023, nearly 6
million vinyl records were sold, the highest figures since 1990. With this resurgence came increased
consumer expectations for high-quality playback equipment. Rega needed to create a turntable that
not only met these expectations but exceeded them. The primary challenges included:
* **Design Innovation**: Developing a turntable with a revolutionary design that would capture the
attention of discerning audiophiles.
* **Material Selection**: Choosing materials that would enhance sound quality while maintaining a
stylish and contemporary look.
* **Vibration Dampening**: Ensuring the turntable could effectively dampen vibrations to deliver a
pristine audio experience.

### **The Solution**

Rega turned to Kewell Converters for our expertise in precision foam engineering, more specifically
[acoustic foam][59]. We supplied the specialised foam required for the Rega RP8 Turntable, playing a
crucial role in its innovative design and functionality. Key elements of the solution included:
* **Revolutionary Plinth Design**: The RP8 features a new plinth design, incorporating carefully
conceived and fabricated materials supplied by Kewell Converters. This design is low-mass yet
highly rigid, ensuring minimal vibration and maximum sound clarity.
* **RB808 Tonearm**: The turntable comes equipped with the RB808 tonearm, known for its precision
and stability.
* **24v Low Voltage Motor**: Controlled by a custom-built, hand-tuned electronic power supply, this
motor ensures consistent and low-vibration performance.
* **Triple Layered Float Glass Platter** and **Planar 9 Hub Bearing Assembly**: These components
contribute to the turntable’s superior sound quality and aesthetic appeal.
* **Vibration Dampening**: The foam supplied by Kewell Converters effectively dampens vibrations,
further enhancing the audio experience.

### **Results**

The collaboration between Rega and Kewell Converters produced outstanding results, transforming the
Rega RP8 Turntable into a market-leading product. Key outcomes included:
* **High Performance**: The turntable’s design, incorporating Kewell Converters’ foam, achieved a
perfect balance of low mass and high rigidity, resulting in exceptional sound quality.
* **Enhanced Aesthetics**: The contemporary skeletal design of the RP8 was made possible by the
compact yet [high-performance][60] foam used in its construction.
* **Vibrational Control**: The specialised foam and low-vibration motors ensured that vibrations
were effectively dampened, allowing for a superior listening experience.
* **Industry Recognition**: The Rega RP8 was praised as “one of the best designs of all time” by
renowned designers Sir Jony Ive and Marc Newson, cementing its status as a top-tier turntable.

### **Conclusion**

The partnership between Rega and Kewell Converters exemplifies the power of [collaboration][61] and
innovation. By leveraging Kewell Converters’ expertise in precision foam engineering, Rega was able
to overcome significant challenges and create a turntable that stands out in the competitive market
of vinyl playback equipment. The Rega RP8 Turntable not only meets but exceeds consumer
expectations, offering an unparalleled audio experience and earning accolades from industry leaders.

Looking ahead, Rega and Kewell Converters are committed to continuing their partnership, exploring
new ways to push the boundaries of audio technology.

Ready to experience the difference that precision engineering can make? Contact Kewell Converters
today to learn more about our innovative solutions and how we can help elevate your products to the
next level.
